meta.title: 1962 Canadian BCP, lectionary and appointment rules
meta.description: Rule records for the 1962 Daily Office. The resolver in src/lib/content/bcp1962.ts applies these rules in code; the records document intent and support validation.

sources.ref: The Book of Common Prayer (1962), notes to the Table of Lessons, the Order how the Psalter is Appointed, and the General Rubrics
sources.note: Transcribed from the official ACC PDF during plan curation; see PROVENANCE.md.

rules.summary: When the First Sunday in Advent falls in an even year, read Year I for the whole ecclesiastical year; in an odd year, read Year II.
Verses in the Table of Lessons are stated inclusively.
Verses printed within brackets are permissive additions to the appointed passages.
A letter a or b after a verse number signifies the first or second part of that verse.
When a Lesson begins with a pronoun, the reader substitutes the appropriate noun.
Appointed propers for Sundays and holy days override the ordinary weekday lessons.
A holy-day falling on certain Sundays keeps its own Collect, Epistle, and Gospel, with the Sunday Collect said after it.
Holy-days on Sundays in Advent or Lent, Ash Wednesday, or Ascension Day transfer to the following Tuesday; other transfer cases are listed in calendar-rules.json.
On Septuagesima, Sexagesima, or Quinquagesima the Purification displaces the Sunday service; the Conversion of St Paul and St Matthias transfer to Tuesday.
If there is one additional Sunday before the Sunday next before Advent, use the Sixth Sunday after Epiphany; if two, use the Fifth and Sixth.
On Trinity XXI to XXVI the minister may use canonical first lessons in place of the Apocrypha; second lessons are unchanged.
The Psalter is read through once a month as appointed, unless one of the tables following is used.
On the thirty-first day, use the thirtieth day's psalms or one of the twenty-four selections.
On a weekday with no proper psalms, one psalm may be omitted provided one psalm or one numbered portion is retained.
Psalm 119 is appointed by numbered parts; each part is eight verses, part N covering verses 8N-7 through 8N.
Ember Days are the Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday after Advent III, Lent I, Whitsunday, and Holy Cross Day.
Rogation Days are the Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday before Ascension Day.
